utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Please be seated. Good morning ladies and gentlemen. Good morning to the technical booth, the interpreters, registry staff, counsel for the Prosecution, counsel for the Defence. We are resuming our proceedings. Before we do so, I should like to ask Mr. Jovan Simic what news he has for us about Mr. Prcac.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Mr. Prcac is present, as you can see. I still haven't managed to get in touch with Mr. McFadden. I was told to call him today after 9.30, and I hope that we will be able to overcome the problem together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Simic. Madam Registrar, have you sent the transcript from yesterday to the President of the Tribunal, the part I asked you to send to him, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I did yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So I think that now we can continue with the actual hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. I wish to remind you that you are still testifying under oath, and now you will continue to answer questions put to you by Mr. Waidyaratne. Mr. Waidyaratne, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber when you were mobilised in 1992 during the conflict, were you at any time injured or wounded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: If I say that it was on the 30th of May, 1992, is it correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What happened, very briefly, if you can say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The attack on Prijedor was going on. I was in the police station. I went out in front of the building, and a guy threw a grenade and wounded me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How long were you hospitalised?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For five or six days. They took out a fragment from my back, a shell fragment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, during this time, in your evidence you said you were transferred to be the assistant driver or the assistant to the driver of the van. When was this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was after the 25th of April, prior to the attack on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, you spoke about the night that a mass killing took place in Keraterm, and you said that you were on duty either from 6.00 or 7.00 in the evening till the next morning. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From 9.00 on the 24th until 7 a.m. on the 25th. That would be my regular shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: In the evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 9.00 in the evening, yes, the whole night until 7 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that the duty officer informed you that there was a telephone call from the Keraterm camp around 12.00 or 12.15 in the night as there was some -- as they wanted some help. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't inform me. He informed the driver on duty, and as I was his assistant, we went off together.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, it was only you and the driver?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: First, who was duty officer who informed you? Who was on duty that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the duty officer of that shift?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: The person who informed or conveyed the message to you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The driver of the police van.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, let me understand you correctly, was the driver who was the duty officer at the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the driver on duty, and the officer on duty tells him, and I go with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, be very clear, who was the officer who was on duty who informed the driver?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed by the driver, with whom I went, and he was informed by the person on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Bosancic. I just want to -- can you tell the name of the driver?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The driver of the police van?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Tomo Stojakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Who was the person who informed him? What's his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday who was the leader of the shift. So as to avoid repeating the name, I told you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You want to go to a private session to make it clear to have the name? Do you want to go to a private session?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: May I very briefly, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne, I think the witness gave you an answer yesterday. The witness asked for a private session to answer that question. He gave you his answer yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I'm correct, he gave the name -- to clarify things, but he gave the name of the commander. To see as to whether this commander and the duty officer was the same person, may I have your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in public session now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when he informed -- the duty officer informed you about the telephone call from Keraterm, did he say as to what exactly -- what you had to do or what you're supposed to do when you go there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I obey orders from the driver, and the driver told me that I should accompany him and that we should go and see what was going on, that we should drive to the spot and inform the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: This driver was a colleague of yours, isn't he, a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: He gave you orders. Did he say as to what you will have to do -- what you had to do when you go to the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know as to what you had to do when you go to Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My duty was to provide security for the vehicle and the driver, so I was his escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you went to Keraterm camp and parked the vehicle near the weighing machine; am I correct? Now, then you said a person around 50 to 60 years old came and spoke to you and said that he requested for reinforcements. Did you know this person, the person who spoke to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was he a policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Didn't you think that it was necessary for you to know as to who this person was, as to what he was doing in the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did the driver, the other police officer who went with you, tell you as to who -- whether he knew this person who spoke to you and him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite sincere, when in the middle of the night you come to such a place and you're approached by an unknown person, you feel afraid and you want to get away as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: But Mr. Bosancic, I thought you were a policeman who went there to provide some assistance to the people who requested your presence there. Am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am a reserve policeman. Never in my life was I a policeman. It's another matter when somebody is trained to be a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you, if I understood you correctly, you were there to provide even security for the person, the driver, isn't it? You were armed, were you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my duty anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were scared. Did you get scared by seeing this 50- to 60-year-old man? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got scared when I heard the Muslims thumping and singing, and I was also afraid of this man. You can imagine an elderly man in his 50s wearing a very old uniform which was not worn any more regularly, a cloth uniform, and I felt afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So you didn't stay there for long immediately. You made a semi-circle, and according to your testimony, you all came back to the police station. That's your position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when you came to the police station, according to your testimony yesterday, you said that you straight away went to rest. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Didn't you think that it was your duty, your obligation, especially because you said that you were scared and you saw some unknown person, that it was your duty to report this matter to the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The driver who was driving and who was on duty, he goes to inform him, not me. An active-duty policeman, he informs the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Didn't you think that you had an obligation to inform?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne, the witness has already answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I would move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I would move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So your position is immediately after you returned, you went to rest. Until 6.00 in the morning you were resting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that. Six, 6.30, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you get to know as to whether any reinforcements were sent from the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the police station in the centre of town, and for Keraterm, the police station number two at Urije was responsible, so most probably the -- my duty officer would have had to contact the commander of police station number two and then to see what should be done, that it was none of my business to interfere.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you get to know as to whether the reinforcements were sent or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, the next day morning you said the duty officer came and said that there was a bad situation in Keraterm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tomo told me, the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me last night there was some trouble up there. He woke me up, and I was curious to see what was happening, and I asked the duty officer whether I could go and see, and then he said, "Don't get too close. Just go and look around."

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bosancic, I thought you now -- please, make me understand this. You were on duty from 9.00 in the night, and you go to rest. You're allowed to, you're allowed to rest during your duty shift, is it? You went to the next building into the basement and rested, according to you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am the assistant. I am called in only exceptionally. It was my own curiousity that prompted me to ask the driver to take me to Keraterm to see what was happening. There are cases when the driver goes alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So it's your keenness that made you, or that you were on duty made you go with the driver. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, the second time, in the morning, did the driver of the vehicle tell you -- you used the word "trouble." What exactly did he tell you mean by "trouble"? What had happened in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The officer on duty passed on to him that something had happened in Keraterm that night. Whether he had been in touch with Police Station II or just with him, I don't know, but we asked to go and see what was happening. It was our initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, to make it very clear, before you went to Keraterm, did you know as to what has happened in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So you were keen, and according to your testimony yesterday, you insisted that you go again to the Keraterm camp in the morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am a conscientious person and a man of good character in life, and that is what prompted me, and that is why I was interested to see what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: In the morning again, according to your testimony, you went there in the morning with the same driver who went with you in the night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And the second time when you then went there to the Keraterm camp, you didn't stay there much? How long did you stay?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Briefly. We just made a circle. We got as far as the weighing machine, made a circle. No one approached us. We saw people washing, and I thought to myself, "Let's get out as soon as possible." As soon as I saw those sneakers and pieces of clothing, I realised that something terrible must have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You returned back to the police station and did nothing with regard to what you saw.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bosancic, you spoke about a Serbian holiday. Can you exact -- explain as to -- what this holiday in August, very briefly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a religious holiday observed on the 19th of August. It is transfiguration when water turns into fire and ice, and this is according to the Bible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on this day, you were working attached to the Prijedor Police Station I. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is where I was always working because that was the station on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Bosancic, according to your testimony yesterday, you received a report about a shooting in Gomjenica. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The driver on duty was called up by the duty officer, and he said that, "You guys go up there. Something is going on. There's some shooting there."

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Gomjenica has a police station there, and it has a commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So when you received this police -- the report or the information, you go again to Gomjenica -- I'm sorry, to Gomjenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Gomjenica, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know before you left as to what place that you had to go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told us on the right-hand side. That is what they said on the phone, and he's a professional driver, so he knows where he has to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was it the same person whom you gave the name earlier, your colleague?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bosancic, please recall this incident. When you went to this place, did you see a checkpoint, a temporary checkpoint, there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the right-hand side. We had to pass through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: If I can call it a Serb checkpoint, is it correct, it was manned by Serb people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you come to -- during your inquiry, did you come to know a person by the name of Rajko?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was he alleged to have shot Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: During your inquiry, did you see a young boy there named Zeljko Zoka [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Zeljko Sikic, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see the vehicle which Mr. Zigic is alleged to have travelled?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see another person by the name of Dragan or Dosen, Goran Dosen, a person there, who was an accomplice or a friend of Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that that was his surname. I'm not sure about his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Dosen there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was lying on the ground as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was he injured?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had been beaten. There was some blood, but not as badly as Zoran.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you inquire as to why he was beaten?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You went for an inquiry, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty driver was there. I didn't want to interfere, to get involved, or somebody to shoot at me, Rajko or someone else. I wanted to stay clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: As a policeman, even as a bystander, didn't you inquire as to what happened there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot understand that he was a sniper. There were 20 people there, and he shot at their heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bosancic, you're confusing this. According to your knowledge, was Dosen a person who has come with Mr. Zigic in that car?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dosen was lying on the ground together with Zigic. Who was in the car, I don't know. I didn't see the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you get to know that there was some jewellery, money, in the possession of the people with Mr. Zigic during that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne, please watch the time. I will let you know when the time comes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, if I may check, is it five minutes, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You already overstepped your time. It was half an hour for today. We started at 9.25. Remember, you had three-quarters of an hour. You used a quarter of an hour yesterday, so logic tells us you have two quarter-of-an-hour periods today. Mr. Deretic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in principle, we would not object, but I would like to notify the Chamber that we have two more witnesses waiting for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's true. We know that. But we have rules. So Mr. Waidyaratne, wind it up. It's what I have always told you, Mr. Waidyaratne. You have limited time. If you have important questions, ask them at the beginning. Otherwise, you're risking not having time to put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you get to know during your presence there, or even after, that Mr. Zigic was in possession of jewellery, money, there? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you get to know during your presence there, there was a female by the name of Senela?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You didn't see a female there at the time that you went there, by the name of Senela?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some women, there were elderly, local women standing there around them, around Rajko, and while they were bloodied on the ground, there were people around them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: My last question, Mr. Bosancic, why did you go to this place? Being present there, did you take any person into custody? Yes or no, did you take --

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't. We couldn't take him into custody. We were going to put Zigic and this other into the police van, but the people from the Gomjenica Police Station wouldn't let us because that is where the incident took place, and they stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Why did you say -- I'm sorry, why did you say that you were going to take Mr. Zigic and the other person into the police van? For what reason? Why did you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we saw them on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Was it the reason that you were going to put them into the police van?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To take them to the police station, the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: As suspects?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to take them. And we thought we could come to some kind of an agreement with the policeman who was there, but we didn't find him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would conclude my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Mr. Waidyaratne. Mr. Deretic, have you any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, I do. And I shall need about 15 minutes to ask my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, after the takeover of power in Prijedor, you said yesterday that you would see Zoran Zigic at the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Immediately after the takeover of power, did you see him wearing a police uniform at any time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps once or twice, but otherwise, he was wearing camouflage uniform all the time. Perhaps the first time, when we all had to have it, he might have had it too, the police-type uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said militiaman's uniform. What do you mean? What colour was this uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was light blue, shirt, trousers, tie.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were taking the detainees to the investigation centre in the police van, who took over the persons you brought in and who did you hand them over to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The driver did. The driver handed the people over, and I think that he handed them over to the inspectors who worked there, depending of the centres we were taking them to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did the driver hand them over -- did the handover take place beside the van or did he do this in the buildings and the rooms there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did it in the rooms, in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: During that time, while this was going on, did you escort the driver and the people who had been detained?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said that on the 29th of April, you were mobilised into the reserve police force in the Prijedor Police Station; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Before that, were you ever in the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have any contact at all previously with the police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After you were mobilised, did you attend any training for a reserve policeman of any kind?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After you were mobilised, did anybody talk to you about the organisational structure of the police force?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, if you can see on the screen, there was a question you asked and the interpreters did not hear the answer. Could you have that answer repeated, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Once again, let me ask you, after you were mobilised, did you attend any training of any kind for reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no training of any kind, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know the organisational structure and chain of command in the police station of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is the commander, and he has his associates, assistants.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know the authorisations of the komandir or commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the authorisations of his assistants were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: As an escort to the police van driver, what were your duties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My duties were to protect the driver and to protect the vehicle, the police van, the Black Maria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On those occasions, were you armed when you were in the police van driving, being driven?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: If you were not in the field with the vehicle, where were you otherwise if you -- when you were doing your duty or shift?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would either be in the vehicle or in a corridor or by the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Which corridor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the corridors of the police station. We had our own bench, and the active-duty police officers had their own room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, following whose orders did -- were the detainees taken to the investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On orders from the inspector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the officer on duty in the hall calls the driver, and if I am standing by the car, he comes to fetch him. He goes up to the inspector and takes over the individual, the person, and he receives a written order for that person to be taken to the centre. Then he would take the person into the van and drive him off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, did you ever personally receive an order from an inspector or the duty officer to transport anyone to the investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were you present when these orders were issued to the driver?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday Mr. Zeljko Meakic. Do you happen to know at that time what his function was, what duty did he perform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander in Omarska for security and the complete police security there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: In the Omarska area, was there a Prijedor police station department?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And what did he provide security for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether -- and a link to the investigation centre of Omarska, whether he had people over which he had immediate command; that is to say, were they policemen who lived and worked in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was he the commander of just those people, those policemen in Omarska at the time, just them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said you were injured on the 30th of May, if I'm right, after a bomb was thrown. Who threw the bomb and where was it thrown?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bomb was thrown at the door, in front of the door of the police station when I was just coming out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was that at the police station centre in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know who threw the bomb?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, allegedly, it was a guy from Puharska. I didn't see him because I became unconscious. I lost consciousness, but the other people who saw the person through the window say they knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know what ethnicity the guy was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When my learned friend of the Prosecution asked you a moment ago, you said you were transferred to provide security for the van on the 25th of April, 1992, after the attack on Prijedor. Tell us, please, when was the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 30th, the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: But you said the 25th of April, 1992, after the attack on Prijedor. You said April.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it means -- that was a slip of the tongue. I got mixed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you were assigned to provide security for the van?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 25th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the duty officer. You used the two terms for one person. You said "duty officer" and you said "komandir," commander. In your mind, are those two terms the same thing? Do they mean the same thing to you, because at one point you said the "duty officer" and on another occasion you referred to him as being the "komandir," commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's the same thing. He's the superior on the shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: That particular individual -- although you've already given me a answer, so let me rephrase the question. That particular individual, did he convey to the driver, did he tell the driver what you were supposed to do while you were doing your shift, your on-duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know who the commander of the reserve police force in Prijedor was? If you do, please tell us; if not, say no.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And I just have two more questions for you, Witness. After you came from Keraterm the second time in the morning hours, do you know whether the driver submitted a report to the person on duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know if a written report was compiled?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, an official note. It was his duty to write an official note and to hand it over to the person on duty, the commander of the shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And my last question, Witness: You said a moment ago that it was your intention to take Zigic and the other person that you came across on the road to the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Now, why did you do this? Why did you want to take him in there? What did you intend to do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't take him in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Yes, but had you taken him in, would you have had to do anything, and what was the purpose of you taking him in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we wanted to take him in and the two -- them in and the person who had shot with the sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would a statement have been taken from those people afterwards about the shooting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And my last question: After that, would those people have been taken for medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes, they would, because Zigic needed medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Deretic. Judge Fouad Riad -- I beg your pardon, Mr. Krstan Simic has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have a few questions myself for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to Mr. Simic asking any questions because there was nothing from the cross-examination which transpired with regard to his -- the accused whom he is representing, and he didn't even ask questions from this witness when the opportunity was given to him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Mr. Krstan Simic can go ahead and ask his questions and you will have an opportunity to respond, Mr. Waidyaratne. But Mr. Krstan Simic, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bosancic, you mentioned an individual by the name [redacted]. Was that a professional policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know, do you know what his professional duties were, function was, in the basic police station of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, do you have an objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The name was mentioned, and it was mentioned in closed session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krstan Simic, we're going to move into private session, and then you can go ahead with your questions, and we're going to have that stricken from the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have completed my -- what I wanted to ask in private, so there's no need to go into private session now. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going to have it struck from the record. Mr. Waidyaratne, do you have a response?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one more question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krstan Simic, you said that you finished, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I meant was with private session. I had asked what I wanted to ask and didn't need a private session any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, then, but please go ahead quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday that you transferred Mr. Nusret Sivac in the police van, that you transported him. Was that to the police station of Prijedor, or did you take him to the collection centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From home to the centre. From the pharmacy next to which he lives to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the answer did not -- was not recorded in the transcript, the answer that we had -- that should have been given in private session, so can we go back into private session, please, for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let us move into private session. Ms. Susan Somers has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to ask for a clarification of the Chamber's ruling on order of examination. My understanding was that there had to be an indication at the time or prior to an examination that particular Defence counsel, other than the one whose case is up now, wanted to examine. It appears that there's a deviation now from that practice. And I'd like to ask the Chamber to clarify whether there's an expansion of the Chamber's ruling now allowing cross-examination based on the cross-examination of the Prosecution. It is very unclear, and we need to have some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well, Ms. Susan Somers. The question was a very simple one. If the Prosecution follows the examination-in-chief part as a whole, we are not going to have any problems. As you know, the Chamber took a flexible interpretation of the rule and allows the Prosecutor to ask questions which were not asked in the examination-in-chief. That is to say, in the cross-examination by the Prosecution, questions may arise which were not posed in the examination-in-chief, and so he has the justification of asking questions only after the cross-examination. Now, the lady's name was brought up during the cross-examination and so Mr. Simic wanted to respond to that. The basic rule of the Chamber, ruling of the Chamber, is that we must respect the equality of arms of both parties and always to respect the principle of adversarial -- the adversarial principle; what you accord to one side, you accord to the other side. Now, if you're going to interpret the ruling very strictly, we can do that too. But, the broad sense of the rule is what we wish. So we are going to authorise Mr. Krstan Simic to go ahead and ask his question but we said that the Prosecution may respond to Mr. Simic's questions, and I don't think there is any infringement of the rules and principles there, which lead us to the product which we wish to achieve, and that product is justice.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krstan Simic, you may proceed and ask your last question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't need a private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. No. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, with the court's indulgence, I should like to comment on the position taken by Madam Prosecutor. I am not an advocate of the Trial Chamber, and I must say that the questioning of a witness, the examination of a witness, who is a layman, absolute layman, in police terms, but this gave rise to the fact that the Prosecution, throughout the entire time of the cross-examination, they used up their time questioning this witness about the structure and organisation of the police force, the chain of command in the police force, and I consider that this kind of examination in the narrow -- basically gave us the right to cross-examine, with all due respect to the flexibility of the Trial Chamber, which always wishes to ensure the equality of arms in the cause of justice. But this particular example has shown us that we need not mention a name, whereas the other side does have an interest in cross-examining. Thank you, Your Honour. And now I go on to my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: The individual that you mentioned a moment ago, do you happen to know what his work post was in the Prijedor Police Station? What position did he occupy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who you're thinking of.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the person you mentioned -- we mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We mentioned an individual by a name and surname, and he was a -- his name was protected. What was his post in the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was in charge of everything. He issued orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You mean the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We are not talking -- we have to go into private session, Mr. President. This is too complicated this way. May we please move into private session at this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: One question because -- with regard to the question put --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. As a follow-up question, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: In public session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Bosancic, please make it clear. In cross-examination I asked a question about a person by the name of Nusret Sivac. I may have misunderstood you. Can you tell us as to -- you said that you transported him in the van. Where did you take him? Did you take him from the police station to the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I took him from the pharmacy which was by his house to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Judge Fouad Riad, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Bosancic good morning. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I just would like to have a better understanding of some of your answers, a few ones. I just -- you mentioned sometime ago this morning - yes, I believe it was this morning - that you are being a very conscientious person, you wanted to see what happened in the camp, after the shooting and you went again with Tomo, the driver. Now, you wanted to know what was -- what happened, so you went -- but you went as far as the weighing machine and turned back after seeing -- after realising that something terrible had happened and you turned back immediately, did not stay. What made you understand it was so terrible? You went -- you went to know what was happening, so what did you discover?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you see people washing down a pista and you see sneakers scattered about and bits of clothing, jackets, and things like that, you know something terrible has happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So you saw blood around. Did you see corpses, dead people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But you saw blood, people washing blood?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were washing the pista. I wasn't close by. I could just see them washing the pista, and I saw scattered -- clothing scattered about. I saw bits of clothing, parts of track suits, sneakers, all thrown about, scattered around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was that what made you realise that something terrible had happened and you just ran away, turned back, or was there something more for you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: It was completely silent. Nobody was saying anything. They were just looking at each other silently, and you can see that something had had to have happened. This dead silence. It was an eerie silence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you that something terrible had happened which made you turn back immediately? This turning back was sudden. You didn't go for that. You went to find out, and you turned around and went back immediately.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So what was so dreadful?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was terrible to see these elderly people quiet, their heads bent down, to see people washing the pista and to see all this clothing scattered around and everything -- everybody silent, nobody was saying a word. And straight away I saw that something was wrong and I said, "Tomo, there's something wrong here. Something's not quite right. Let's leave as quickly as possible." Nobody coming up to us, so I thought let's get out of here as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Perhaps in the same spirit, you said that when you transferred, you took people, if I remember rightly, from the police station to the camps after their interview at the police station. Then when you were asked by the Prosecutor if you have seen any injured people, you said, "I did not like to look." Was that also because there was something terrible and you, in the same line, you refuse to look at something terrible?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was like this: I had seen a lot of things, things that normal people don't get a chance to see. And I didn't want to be present, to be there when the people got into the police van, because I was a sportsman and I was well-known around town. Lots of people knew me and I knew lots of people. And yesterday when I was asked by the Prosecutor for somebody's name, he should have continued and rounded up his thought. He asked about my child's kum or godfather. It doesn't matter who it was but that's who he was asking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: If you refuse to look, is it already because you have a notion, an idea, that these people might be injured, might look bad? Or otherwise, why would you refuse to look?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. Just a simple question. You said that -- when you were asked if you saw Mr. Zigic when you went to the camps, you said you were there for a short time, but if Zigic was there, you would have seen him because he would come up immediately to the van, if he was there. Is that because you thought that Zigic was the man who was the man in charge, who would communicate with the people coming and was an important man in the place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he wasn't an important man, but when the policeman comes to these collection centres, then everybody comes up to it. Everybody comes up to see who we've brought in. People are interested in seeing who we've brought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So you thought you would come out of interest but not because of responsibility. Out of curiosity, you mean? Just -- that was your guessing? Because you were very affirmative. You said he would come out.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had he been there, he would have come out. Because the people there guarding would come up to see who was in the van. Everybody's interested in seeing. Not only with bad intentions. There were people that knew people. So there were acquaintances, relationships of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mean all the simple guards, all the people around would just come out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not everybody, not everybody would come out. It depends of the centre we were going to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And of the importance of the person or his role in the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me explain. The driver knew best who was coming out. The driver knew who was coming up to him and to whom he was going to hand people over to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Fouad Riad. Judge Wald, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that you had no prior experience with the police structure or police service before you were mobilised in this particular time, and I think Mr. Simic's questions or comments, which you heard, emphasised that. My question therefore is, if that's true, and this really was your first experience in the police, and you had no training, no special training, after you came in, how were you able to know, in answer to the -- Mr. Deretic's question, that Commander Meakic only was in command of the Omarska Police Station personnel? I mean, you told us you knew he was commander, but I'm just Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 wondering how you got the knowledge of what his specific authority was in the camp, if, as you pointed out, you really had no background in police structure or in police experience before then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I worked in a police station which was the main police station and was superior to all others, and we hear these things from other people talking. From the policemen, I'm referring to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So you heard, if I understand your answer correctly, you heard from police in the police station where you worked that Meakic was the commander of Omarska police personnel, Omarska Police Station, police personnel at Omarska. Was that all you heard? Did you hear about the authority of anybody else in the camp, of any of the other personnel in the camp? Through the same means, through just what you heard at the Prijedor police station.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Meakic was the only person you heard anything about in terms of their authority at the Omarska Police Station; is that right? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I wanted to get a couple of things straight because I was somewhat confused by what appeared to be slightly different answers. In terms of who ordered the people to the centre, did I understand your testimony to be correct that before somebody was taken from the police station out to the Omarska centre, there had to be an order from the inspector which was given to the duty officer who gave it to the driver? Was that correct, or did I misunderstand it? Did you say, in other words, today that there had to be an order for a person to go to the Omarska centre that came from the inspector?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the police station there's a duty officer in the hall who communicates with the driver and with the office of the inspector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: When you say office of the inspector, is that the office of the inspector at Omarska, or were there inspectors in the police station? I'm just trying to get -- understand. Were the inspectors who gave the orders to the duty officers, were they in the police station or were they the inspectors out in the Omarska centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So there were -- just to make sure we have it straight now. There were inspectors in the police station. Were they the ones who interrogated people first in the police station before they were sent on to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. And they -- they were the ones who decided who would be sent on to Omarska or Keraterm, wherever?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us say that that was so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in terms of your two very brief visits out to Keraterm, on the first evening or the first visit, which I guess was after midnight, you said was in response to a telephone call that had come in apparently from the Keraterm to the police station, and you and the driver went out to see what was happening out there. Do you know whether the duty officer or the driver or anyone else told -- called out to Keraterm and said, "Well, the van is coming out"? In other words, was there any communication that you know about that told anybody out at Keraterm that you were coming out there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't much communication on something like that. He would speak to the driver. I was in the corridor. The driver would come up and say, "Let's go." "Where are we coming?" "We're going to Keraterm, they're calling," and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Twice in your testimony, both as to the evening visit and I think as to the morning visit afterwards, you talked about only or principally seeing elderly people, and I was somewhat confused about this because a lot of the testimony we've had suggested that for the most part, the detainees in both Keraterm and Omarska tended to be men in the military-age area. But was -- I just wanted to confirm that that was your testimony, that you saw principally, both in the evening visit and in the morning visit, or at least you only referred to elderly people, is that right? Did I hear you right that it was primarily older people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you, younger men and the strong men were needed on the front. Elderly people, 40s, in their 40s and 50s, would accept to guard -- would accept guard duty rather than going to the front, because I would know them. Prijedor is a small town. I knew people, a lot of people. And when you see a man at midnight with a moustache and armed and wearing an old uniform, it's better not to have anything to do with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So you are telling us that the elderly people that you saw at Keraterm on the evening visit, and also you mentioned them in the morning, were they the ones doing the cleanup of the pista?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: They were. So you're telling us that those elderly people, to your knowledge, were guards out there. They weren't detainees, they were guards?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The detainees probably couldn't be walking around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay, I just --

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were wearing these old uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I just wanted to know which, in your impression, that they were. And you were -- you said you were -- they were old people, old is a comparative term, but anyway, they were old people, and because the younger ones had all had to go to the front, and they were armed and wearing old uniforms, and it's better not to have anything to do with him, but you're talking about one of these elderly people. Just explain that a little bit. Why would an older person -- you might think that older person wasn't terribly efficient, but why would you be afraid to deal with him if he was performing some form of guard duty at the camp? Because he was armed and you thought he might not know how to use his arms, or what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, the way a man approaches you, the way he looks when he comes up to the vehicle and starts talking to you, you see that something is wrong with him, and he's got a rifle. And as to your previous question about older and younger men, even women manned checkpoints sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I'm familiar with that, thank you. I have a few more questions. I want to understand a little bit better about what you did see in those brief periods in the evening visit, the after-midnight visit and the morning visit, but primarily the after-midnight visit at Keraterm when you and the driver of the vehicle went out and spent that very brief period, never got out of the vehicle, and turned around and came back. I believe you said once, I think twice, that your impression was that it was Muslim detainees "singing and thumping," I think those were words that you used. My question was, and I'm now talking about the midnight, the after-midnight visit, were these Muslims that were singing and thumping, were they inside the building or were they outside the building, or, I mean, where were they when you heard them singing and thumping?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside, inside, inside the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. What was happening outside the building at that time? Was any shooting going on at the time you saw -- during the brief period you were there? Because we all know from testimony that during the night, we've had everybody, including Defence witnesses, tell us that there was sporadic and, later, intense shooting. I'm simply asking you whether during the brief period you were there you saw or heard any shooting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Were there guards outside of the buildings that -- where the thumping and singing was going on? Yes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Did the guards, were the guards armed? Did the guards have any machine-guns? Was there a machine-gun, whatever, standing machine-gun in the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- when we were turning the vehicle around ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Go ahead. You said, "I didn't see it, but when we were turning the vehicle around," what?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were about to turn around, we saw a couple of men, and they were armed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. And they were -- am I right, they were in front of the building where the singing and thumping was coming from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. So if, I'm just -- this may sound like repetition, but I'm sure you understand that Judges have to be able to understand in their own mind the testimony of all witnesses, so I just want to make sure I understand. You turned around and went home -- went home, sorry, back to the police station that night. Then in the morning voluntarily, just because you wanted to know what happened, you and the driver came back to Keraterm. Again, my question would be: Did anybody, to your knowledge, tell people in Keraterm you were coming back in the morning, or you just went without, to your knowledge, their knowing that you were coming?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't know we were coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay, okay. You went back and then you looked around, saw the cleaning of the pista going on and the remnants of sneakers and jackets, et cetera, going on, and then you turned around and went back, and your driver made a written report, if I understand your testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, an official report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. And that, as far as you know, was the end of the involvement of either you or the driver in anything that happened at Keraterm. There was no follow-up that you knew about to the report; is that right? Nobody ever questioned you about the report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me, no. The driver stayed behind, my replacement came, and I left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. I have one last question, again, that I want to make sure that I know what your final answer is because there seems to be some confusion. When you and the driver would drive, would drive detainees from the police station to the camps, at one point yesterday you said that usually the commanders would -- would take charge of the prisoners or the detainees. They'd be handed over by your driver to the detainees [sic]. Today I think you said that it was usually the inspectors, that the driver would take the detainees into -- and hand them over inside some building to the inspectors. I'm wondering now which or both of those statements would you say right now was the most accurate one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The driver would hand them over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: To whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the officer on duty. It could either be the inspector coming downstairs or someone else, or they may have communicated by telephone, or they may have used a Motorola and let them know that we were coming. They had a radio station in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand the communication, but still, it's important for me to understand this answer, that when you drove up on all your various trips, but let's concentrate on Omarska, the prisoners would be handed over to, are you saying now, either a commander or an inspector who came from downstairs? Is that, is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the inspector, to the inspector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Always to the inspectors or --

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who was investigating them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: No, I understand. But is that always? That's different from a commander. Yesterday you said commanders, and I think we're all agreed commanders are different from the inspectors.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I told you that I didn't get out of the vehicle, but I know on the way back as we talked, me and the driver.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: As you talked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is from those conversations that I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: That you heard what? I'm just -- it's a simple question. However you heard it, did you hear that it was always inspectors who came and got the prisoners or that they were handed over to; or was it, as your original testimony said, commanders sometimes; or as you said a few minutes ago, maybe duty officers or somebody? I just -- I just want to get the answer.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, the best thing to do was to get away as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: But you said that on the way back the driver would discuss with you, even if you didn't immediately recognise who they were being handed over to. I'm just -- figure if you made a lot of trips there, you must have come away with an impression, whether from the driver or from your own observation, that prisoners were being handed over either to the commander or the inspectors, or always the inspectors. It's that simple.

utterances.speaker: DRAGO BOSANCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I think that I can't tell you with certainty because I didn't get out. But there were different situations. I don't think it was fixed, "You have to give them to the inspector." There weren't any such fixed rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Wald. I think that all the questions have been put to you, and to be the last to speak is my privilege, so I don't have any questions for you. Thank you very much for having come. We wish you a safe journey home, and success in your work. I'm going to ask the usher to accompany you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I am glad to see that the Tribunal is in such distinguished hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I think the moment has come for us to have a break. I should like to share with the parties my concern. We have two more witnesses. It is not possible to sit in the afternoon because we have another case, so perhaps I'm going to ask you to try and find a solution so that we complete these two witnesses today, because if a witness doesn't complete his testimony, we would have to wait and stay until Tuesday. So unless the parties find a solution, the Chamber will have to take things into its own hands. But it appears that Mr. Deretic has a solution already, so please go ahead, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just wanted to note that we have another problem of a technical nature which I think we will have to address, and that is the question of the videolink. We're not working tomorrow, on Friday, or on Monday. Tuesday we begin with a videolink, so I think we have a large number of questions to put to the Chamber from the technical point of view. So we really are short of time, and we will have to address those matters, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was precisely one of the reasons I told the Prosecutor that I was expecting them to make me a present of a little of their time. I am joking, of course. It is their right to use their time. We are fully aware of all this. We will try to give you decisions regarding outstanding issues connected to video conferencing even orally if we don't have a written ruling. We will address those matters today. So we are now going to have a half-hour break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Mr. Deretic, let us begin with the testimony of the next witness. Do you have any suggestions regarding the saving of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we shall do our best. We'll see how we do with the next witness, and after that, things will be quite clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but perhaps we must have at least some orientation. We will see how we do, but within certain limits. My suggestion would be that we distribute the time as follows. We have more or less three hours 40 minutes of work in all left. We are going to take more or less 40 minutes for the lunch break, and after that, we'll have two periods of an hour and a half for each witness. So I would suggest that we distribute the time as follows. This is an effort of synthesis and mental organisation that we need to undertake and it's a good exercise for the future. Forty-five minutes for the Defence, 30 minutes for the Prosecution, 15 minutes for the judges. Those would be guidelines, and we shall try to do that. And I think if all of us make an effort, perhaps we will succeed. It is just an orientation, so please do your best. So we really do have to optimise the time, go directly to the issue, put the important questions to the witness and leave the others aside. Who is the next witness, Mr. Deretic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the next witness is Dragan Stojanovic. Can you hear me? It is just a coincidence that the witness has the same surname as my co-counsel, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Susan Somers? Excuse me. I had the witness brought in not to hear a discussion. The witness is about to make his solemn declaration. Ms. Susan Somers, do you have something important to say? Because if I had known, I would have had the witness wait outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. You were just commenting on the time frame, and I just wanted to ask the Chamber possibly to consider an even distribution of time, instead of 45/30, 37 whatever each, and that I think would probably -- because we have no idea, quite honestly, what the direct will be about until we hear it. We have no background on these witnesses generally, and therefore we have to, as it were, think on our feet in many instances. So if we could -- our preference, of course, for the record, would be an equal distribution of time if the Chamber is so minded. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will follow this orientation, but we'll see at the end. As you know, Ms. Susan Somers, this is not the Prosecution case; this is the Defence case. I don't want to continue the discussion now. If you compare the time the Prosecution took during its case and the time taken by the Defence, you will perhaps see the difference. The Defence never had the same amount of time as the Prosecution. But we'll try, Ms. Susan Somers. This is just an orientation, but that is not really the problem. So let's begin now. Mr. Dragan Stojanovic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please read the solemn declaration given to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. You will first be answering questions which are going to be put to you by Mr. Deretic. So please begin, Mr. Deretic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Will you please identify yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On 7th of May, 1962, in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where are you living today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm an engineer of civil defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity and religion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I am a Serb of Orthodox faith.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, after the war broke out in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, were you a member of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you joined and in which unit did you serve?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From of September, 1991, in the 43rd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Until when were you in that unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Until the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
